Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Afghanistan's response with the bat. Litton Das leads his troops out to the middle as the Bangladeshi players spread out to their fielding positions. The man in form, Sediqullah Atal, will be partnered by Rahmanullah Gurbaz, who is searching for some runs. And interestingly, spin to start with. Nasum Ahmed will open the attack for Bangladesh.  Sediqullah to face. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Bangladesh might feel they left out 15-20 runs, given the way they started off in the Powerplay. And the pressure is rightly on them to defend this total. They have won only 1 out of 4 T20Is at Abu Dhabi and have lost all three of their matches, while defending. But as we all know, these stats don't matter in the present. It is all about putting in a united bowling effort to restrict this buoyant Afghan side, who have a very strong track record of 12 wins out of 17 T20Is at Sheikh Zayed Stadium. Remember, a victory here will seal Afghanistan’s place in the Super 4s, sending them through alongside Sri Lanka and ending Bangladesh’s campaign. For Bangladesh, even a win won’t be enough on its own because of their inferior net run rate. Their only hope then would be for Sri Lanka to defeat Afghanistan in the final match of Group B, keeping the door to qualification ever so slightly open. It is all shaping up to be a cracker of a run chase with so many stakes on the line.

Spin is the king, once again, and this has been proved by a team with a luxury of spin bowling options. They utilised four spinners, and all four dished out deceptive variations that just choked the scoring in that middle phase. The batters couldn't form steady partnerships post Tanzid's wicket and slipped from 87/1 to 121/4. In a combined effort of 13 overs, the spinners gave 98 runs, and shared 4 wickets among them, two each for Noor and skipper Rashid. AM Ghazanfar was a bit on the expensive side. And those efforts were magnificently backed up by the two seamers closing out in the end.

But once Saif was dismissed in Rashid's first over, with that 63-run partnership broken, there was a bit of calm brought in by the tweakers in the middle overs. Bangladesh weren't able to fully capitalise on the kind of launchpad the two Hasans provided early doors as the spin continued to stranglehold. Boundaries dried up and runs did not come at a fair clip, but Tanzid kept sending one or two to the fence on some occasions and got off to his fifty as well. However, with Noor Ahmad coming up trumps and picking up two big wickets, the scoring took a significant dip. And in that 7-15 over phase, Bangladesh could score only 60 runs, losing three big wickets.

With the ball swinging and bouncing, the Bangladeshi openers initially looked like cats on the hot tin roof, failing to get the timing right with a lot of false strokes induced. But once settled, Saif Hassan and Tanzid Hasan found boundaries, albeit surviving a few close calls. Afghanistan didn't bowl poorly at all, but couldn't convert the chances. Hence, the Powerplay went Bangladesh's way. The first three overs went for just 24 runs, but the next three went for 35, with 59/0 on the board, at the end of the field restrictions.

A pleasing finish for Afghanistan with the ball. 5 precious dots, and just 15 runs conceded in the last 2 overs. One key area for improvement for the Afghans was the slog overs bowling-wise, and they have improved in that phase massively in this important clash. Overall, it has been a proper tussle between bat and ball, but with wickets in hand, and still failing to score 10 runs or more in an over, Bangladesh will feel they left out a few runs here.

Looked to be pitching outside leg but Rashid Khan has referred it upstairs. UltraEdge shows no bat involved and the Ball Tracking shows the ball is pitching inside the line and it is projected to smash into the middle stump. A successful review for the Afghans and the on-field decision is overturned. Litton Das departs for 9 (11) and how many times have we seen a wicket falling right after the hydration break? And with wickets in hand, this is a perfect launchpad for Bangladesh to post in excess of 160 or 170, which would be a very good score in this do-or-die clash for them. Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.6: Mohammad Nabi to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker one, full and on leg, Litton Das clips it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.5: Mohammad Nabi to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags his length back, on middle, Litton Das pats it to the right of the bowler, where Nabi gathers it up.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.4: Mohammad Nabi to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Arm ball, full and on middle, angles in, Tanzid Hasan bunts it out towards long on for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.3: Mohammad Nabi to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floats it up, short and on middle, Tanzid Hasan stays back and nudges it with soft hands towards deep mid-wicket and turns around for a risky second run. Rashid Khan is quick to charge in from the deep, picks up and throws it at the keeper's end, but it is just a bit wide and Hasan makes his ground. A direct hit would have gotten him there
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.2: Mohammad Nabi to Tanzid Hasan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter, short and around off, Litton Das moves back and heaves it off the inner half of the bat through mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Mohammad Nabi to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rashid Khan is the leading wicket-taker for Afghanistan against Bangladesh in T20Is. He has now taken 23 wickets in 12 matches. His best is 4/12, with an economy of under 6 and has also picked up 2 four-fors. Spin continues to be in tandem, but 'Mr. President' Mohammad Nabi comes into the attack. He replaces AM Ghazanfar.
Slows it up, full and on off, Litton Das steps across and tucks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Rashid Khan to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted, full and on middle, Litton Das strides out to play but gets an inside edge onto his pads. A slight appeal for LBW, but turned down.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Rashid Khan to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh skipper, Litton Das, is in at 3.

OUT! BOWLED'EM! Rashid Khan gets his man! A much-needed wicket for Afghanistan, and the 63-run opening stand has been broken now. This is another wrong'un, full and on off, keeps a bit low. Saif Hassan goes down to sweep it away but plays all over it and gets nowhere near the ball. It goes under the bat and rattles the off pole. Rashid Khan gives a cold, steely stare at the batter. Saif walks back for a fine 30 off 28, giving the start Bangladesh needed in this big game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Rashid Khan to Saif Hassan, OUT! b Rashid Khan.

Commentary.Commentary: A googly, short and on middle and leg, turns in, Saif Hassan backs away to cut but gets another inside edge towards fine leg for a brace. He has got lucky on a couple of occasions now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Rashid Khan to Saif Hassan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on off, Saif Hassan drives it firmly through extra covers for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Rashid Khan to Saif Hassan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter, short and on middle and leg, Saif Hassan moves back and stabs it out on the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Rashid Khan to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: No wonder as Rashid Khan brings himself into the attack to stem the run flow, and more importantly to provide the breakthrough. He replaces Azmatullah Omarzai.

SIX! HUGE! 19 runs off the over! Loopy delivery, full and on middle, angling in, Tanzid Hasan once again goes down and smokes it powerfully way over the deep square leg fence for half a dozen more. Bangladesh are off to a flier here, and are 59 for no loss at the end of the Powerplay!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: AM Ghazanfar to Tanzid Hasan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: MORE RUNS! AM Ghazanfar follows the batter, bowls this quicker and shorter, on leg. Saif Hassan gets cramped up for room as he tries to cut but gets an inside edge down to fine leg. Fazalhaq Farooqi from short fine chases after it and collects it right before the ropes. Three taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter, full and on middle, Tanzid Hasan eases it to long on for a run. Sensible cricket, and that also brings up the 50 for Bangladesh.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: AM Ghazanfar to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BOOM! Tanzid Hasan goes big now! Flighted, full and on middle and off, turns in a bit. Hasan goes down on one knee and nails the slog sweep with the turn over the deep mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: AM Ghazanfar to Tanzid Hasan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Just when AM Ghazanfar was about to deliver the ball, he loses his grip and the ball drops to his right. Uses a towel to dry it up and is ready to reload.
Fires in a low full toss, on leg, Saif Hassan makes room to drive but gets a bottom edge towards mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air....SAFE! Tossed up, full and around middle, Saif Hassan backs away and tries to go over covers but mistimes it in the air. The ball flies in the air and lands just over the extra cover and cover fielders running backwards. Two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish delivery, angling into the batter, pulled away to deep backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard, on top of middle. Saif Hassan tries to slash it away to the off side, but misses as the ball passes above his angled bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Skilfully played, but at the same time, a brilliant effort in the deep. In vain, though! On a good length, angling into the batter from middle. Saif uses his wrists and short-arm jabs it in front of the square on the leg. Sediqullah Atal from deep backward square leg runs across the circumference of the boundary, to his left, and puts in a dive to flick the ball back in the playing area. The third umpire is summoned to check whether Atal's body is in contact with the ball and the ropes at the same time. After checking several angles very closely it is deemed a boundary. But full marks for the effort from Sediqullah Atal!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: The physio is in for a mandatory concussion check. That bouncer surely rattled Saif Hassan, and he needs a bit of time to recover. He is taking some fluids in as well, and it looks like he is good to continue now.

A well-directed bumper from Omarzai, outside off, with some extra kick off the deck. Saif Hassan is hurried to pull and edges it onto the helmet grille. The ball deflects and flies over the ring toward the deep third fence, where the ball is flicked with a slide by the fielder from the inner ring. Two taken. And there will be a compulsory concussion test for Saif.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, on middle. Tanzid Hasan dances down the track and drills it down, between mid off  and mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Angles it outside off, on a good length with a slight shape away. Tanzid Hasan is forced to poke at it, from the crease and is beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Azmatullah Omarzai to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Will Fazalhaq Farooqi get a third over? Nope, he won't. Change of ends for Azmatullah Omarzai.

Follows the batter, and slides it into the leg stump line on a length. Saif Hassan rocks back but is cramped for space and inside edges it to the short fine leg fielder. Looks to pinch in a single, but it was never there. 8 off AM Ghazanfar's first over. 24 from the last two overs for Bangladesh!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Seeing Hassan dancing down the track, AM Ghazanfar pulls the length back, on middle. All Saif could do is nudge that into the leg side with soft hands.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! That will give him a lot of confidence! That is MASSIVE! Full and pushed through, on middle. Saif Hassan backs away, creates room and hoists it straight down the ground for a cracking 85-meter six into the stands.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Length, on the leg stump. Saif Hassan works it to short mid-wicket off the back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drifting into the batter, on middle and leg. Saif Hassan knocks it straight back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Over the stumps, spinning to the leg stump, on a length. Hassan hangs back and tuckes it to deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: AM Ghazanfar to Saif Hassan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Change? Yes, time for some mystery spin. AM Ghazanfar replaces Azmatullah Omarzai.

FOUR! Two in two for Hasan! Good length, around off, shaping in, takes pace off too. Tanzid Hasan stands tall and pulls it straight down the ground for a boundary to the right of long on. The fourth boundary of the over and Fazalhaq Farooqi's figures read 2-0-19-0.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it through! Tails in a long way, from outside off to the middle stump, on a length. Tanzid Hasan gets a bit across and drives it a bit uppishly, to the right of mid on for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Not a bad review from the Afghans! On a good length, tailing into the batter, around the middle stump, with some bounce. Tanzid Hasan tries to ride the bounce and tuck it across into the leg side, but the ball sneaks past the inside edge and raps on the back pad. A huge appeal for LBW, but not given. Fazalhaq Farooqi looks certain and convinces Rashid Khan to send this one upstairs for a review! Into the forensics now. There is no spike on the UltraEdge as the ball is next to the inside edge. Ball Tracking comes up and shows the ball hitting the top of the leg and middle stumps, on the umpire's call. Afghanistan do not lose the review but this is a tough examination by the bowlers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Edgy, very edgy at the moment, are the Bangladeshi openers! Touch full and shaping away from outside off. Tanzid Hasan gets a bit of a bottom edge and the ball races to the left of the first slip fielder for a boundary at deep third.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: EDGED AND FOUR! The keeper and the first slip fielder are looking at each other and Rashid is not happy one bit. Swinging away from the batter, on a hard length, outside off. Tanzid Hasan gets forward and slashes hard at it, but gets a thick outside edge. The ball shoots flat, between Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Gulbadin Naib. Gurbaz moves a bit to his left but Naib is stationary and the ball races through for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A slip in place. Outswinger, outside off, on a good length. Tanzid Hasan hangs back and tries to cut it square, but plays the ball away from the body and is beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length, outside off. Saif Hassan hops in the crease and steers it with soft hands to the point region. 5 off Omarzai's first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nagging length into the bodyline, nipping in a bit now. Saif Hassan rides the bounce and taps it across into the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: An appeal for caught behind, but not given. Good response by Azmatullah Omarzai! This is on a good length, just outside off, with some extra bounce. Saif Hassan is caught the crease and is forced to poke at it. The ball just nibbles away a bit and beats the outside edge by a kitten-whisker. The UltraEdge later shows no spike.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Hits the deck hard, does Omarzai. Around off on a length. Saif Hassan dances down the track and tries to whack it over the off side, but gets a bit too far to create room and misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! That's more like it! The first boundary of the game for Bangladesh and Saif! Azmat offers it into the slot, full and on middle and leg. Saif Hassan picks it up nicely and whips it over backward square leg. The man from deep square leg runs across to cut it off, but the ball races away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Outside off, on a good length. Saif Hassan flashes at it and hits it straight to the man at point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Reload! A loosener, going down leg, on a length. Saif Hassan misses to glance that away. Wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Azmatullah Omarzai to Saif Hassan, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Azmatullah Omarzai to share the attack. Also, Bangladesh's last 6 opening stands against full-member nations in T20Is have all been in the single digits. Not ideal at all for a team like them.

Tanzid, too, is off the mark. Full and outside off, shaping a shy bit away. Tanzid Hasan gently caresses it between cover and point for a couple of runs. What a questioning opening over from Fazalhaq Farooqi. Just 3 runs off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Tanzid Hasan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! A good effort from Azmatullah Omarzai and had he clung on to that, it would have been a screamer of a catch. Full in length, outside off, Saif Hassan leans into the shot and hits it uppishly to the right of cover. Azmatullah Omarzai leaps and sticks his right hand up. But gets the ball parried behind off the fingertips. A single taken and Saif Hassan is off the mark!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Saif Hassan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Good-length delivery, across off, nipping away. Saif Hassan advances down the track and tries to send the ball to Dubai, but meets only a handful of air.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swings the other way. On a length, outside off, Saif Hassan is beaten all ends up on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Huge appeal for LBW, but the finger stays down. Fazalhaq Farooqi looks confident, but going by Rashid Khan's expressions, he is not very sure about the pitching of the ball. Hence, he does not review it. This swings into the batter very late, on a fuller length, around the leg stump. Saif Hassan plays over the line to flick and is beaten on the inside edge. Gets rapped on the front pad. This looks very close and the replay shows that the ball is pitching inside the line, but the projection shows the ball missing the leg stump. So, a good decision from Rashid to not review it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Farooqui starts off with a peach! Spots Saif charging down the track, Fazalhaq Farooqi slants it wide outside off, across the batter. Saif Hassan misses connecting for a drive on this full ball. Gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! The fans have come in numbers for this crucial clash, and it is pretty evenly matched. We can see the Afghanistan players spread out and take up their respective field positions. First big change for Bangladesh - the opening pair! It is Saif Hassan walking out with Tanzid Hasan. Fazalhaq Farooqi has the new ball in hand as expected and is raring to go with two slips in place as well. Let's play...

The floodlights are on at the beautiful Sheikh Zayed Stadium, and we are moments away from the start. But before that, the players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for the respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first, followed by that of Afghanistan.

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold is pitchside. He says this is the pitch that was used in the last game, and it is a bit dry, but on a closer look, it looks like a fresh wicket. Ravi Shastri joins him and says that there is some grass, but it is brown and burnt. Adds that there is a bit of scarring as well with all the running around. He expects it to be on the slower side but not much turn. Litton said 160 would be an ideal score here, but Ravi reckons they will need 10-15 extra runs to make it a winning score.

Afghanistan (Unchanged Playing XI) - Sediqullah Atal, Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Mohammad Nabi, Gulbadin Naib, Azmatullah Omarzai, Karim Janat, Rashid Khan (C), Noor Ahmad, AM Ghazanfar, and Fazalhaq Farooqi.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Litton Das (C/WK), Saif Hassan (In for Parvez Hossain Emon), Tawhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali, Shamim Hossain, Nurul Hasan (In for Mahedi Hasan), Nasum Ahmed (In for Tanzim Hasan Sakib), Rishad Hossain, Mustafizur Rahman, and Taskin Ahmed (In for Shoriful Islam).

The captain of Afghanistan, Rashid Khan, says they would have batted first as well and wanted to put runs on board. But also adds that it doesn't really matter in T20 cricket, and it is all about playing a good brand of cricket. Highlights that they didn't have too many rest days, as they had to play the first game right after the Tri-Series final. Shares that the boys had a good couple of days off coming into this game. Mentions that they have a good bowling lineup, but also stresses that you still need to bowl well and put the batters under pressure. Adds that they need to hit the right areas and need to come out with a positive mindset. On his fitness, Rashid expresses that he is happy to feel the same way he was feeling before the surgery. Ends by saying he is looking forward to enjoying this game.

The captain of Bangladesh, Litton Das, says that they will bat first. Adds that all the boys are excited to play this game. Mentions that this is the last group game for them and they have to win it. Says that the wicket looks good and 160 would be a ideal score but also expects it to be on the slower side. Tells that they have been playing good cricket in recent times and one bad day doesn't change much for them. Informs that they have made four changes, with Nasum Ahmed, Taskin Ahmed, Nurul Hasan, and Saif Hassan coming into the team, and they are going with three spinners and two pacers.
TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Bangladesh and Litton Das elects to BAT first.

JUST IN - In a big blow to Afghanistan's pace bowling artillery, Naveen Ul Haq, the right-arm seamer, has been ruled out of the Asia Cup due to a shoulder injury. Abdullah Ahmadzai has been named as Naveen's replacement. Ahmadzai made his T20I debut in the recently concluded Tri-Series in Sharjah. More on Naveen, he was declared unfit by the Afghanistan Cricket Board's medical team, and hence, he couldn't make it to the playing XI against Hong Kong, China in the curtain raiser. He will fly back home for an 'intensive rehabilitation and treatment'.

The last time these two sides met was in the 2024 T20 World Cup at Kingstown, where Afghanistan outplayed Bangladesh and stormed into their maiden T20 World Cup semi-final that year. Overall, they also hold a narrow 7-5 lead against Bangladesh, in T20Is. In Abu Dhabi, in this Asia Cup, the record has been even with two wins each for teams batting first and chasing. A win tonight would push Afghanistan to the top of the table while Bangladesh would climb to second. Out of the eight games played so far, only one has truly offered some real competition, so here’s hoping this clash brings the dose of thrill and edge-of-the-seat entertainment the tournament has been missing. Toss and team news coming up shortly.

Bangladesh have been underwhelming so far, especially with the bat. The top order just hasn’t provided the kind of start they would’ve expected. Both Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan have struggled to cross 25 individually, and as a pair, leaving the middle order with the constant task of playing catch-up. Skipper Litton Das has been the standout performer, but he’s often had far too much to shoulder on his own. Even in their win over Hong Kong, China, the chase dragged longer than it should have, costing them a chance to boost their net run rate. The bowling unit has been steady and disciplined across spin and pace, but without runs on the board, their job becomes twice as hard. A few extra from the batters up front could make all the difference. Taskin Ahmed was shockingly rested against Sri Lanka but the seamer will likely be back in the eleven for this important clash.

The Afghans come into this clash fresh from a week’s break and after a commanding 94-run win over Hong Kong, China. Sediqullah Atal has been a shining light at the top, whereas Azmatullah Omarzai continues to be a reliable all-rounder for them. But Rahmanullah Gurbaz is still searching for form with a streak of consecutive low scores, and this might just be the stage for him to fire. With the ball, they continue to grow stronger. Pace has been fiery, but the real edge is the luxury of having so many spin options led by the evergreen Rashid Khan. Few teams in the competition can match that depth, making Afghanistan a challenging prospect under pressure.

As any multilateral tournament heads towards the crunch phase, every single game holds a huge weightage. The same goes for this one as well. As you all know, only two of the four teams from both groups will advance to the Super 4s. It is a do-or-die situation for Bangladesh, as with one win and a humbling defeat, they are positioned in third spot. This is their last league game, and a defeat will knock them out. Whereas Afghanistan still have a couple of games to play, and both are going to be tough ones. But they do have the luxury of winning any one of the two remaining to stay alive. The competition is so tough in this group, as still, three teams can finish at four points, and if that scenario comes into play, the net run rate will be the kingmaker. That’s where Bangladesh are vulnerable, sitting in the negative territory, while Afghanistan currently boasts the best numbers of the lot.

We are back in the city of Abu Dhabi for one of the most important league games of the Asia Cup 2025. Of what is called the group of death by the cricketing pundits, true indeed, the spirited Bangladesh are all set to take on the buoyant Afghanistan at the lavish Sheikh Zayed Stadium. On that note, we welcome you all for our coverage of what is expected to be a thriller of a Group B clash. Great to have you all with us.
... MATCH DAY ...

Bangladesh and Afghanistan are set for a high-stakes clash in Match 9 of the Asia Cup 2025, with both teams looking to strengthen their push for a spot in the next round. Bangladesh opened their campaign with a confident seven-wicket win over Hong Kong, China, where Litton Das anchored the chase with 59, and their bowlers, led by Mustafizur Rahman and Rishad Hossain, showed early promise. However, it all came crashing down against Sri Lanka, which makes this one a must-win game for them. Afghanistan too began with a commanding 94-run victory over Hong Kong, China, powered by Sediqullah Atal’s composed 73 and Azmatullah Omarzai’s blistering fifty, though coach Jonathan Trott has stressed the need for more stability after a mid-innings wobble. This contest promises a fascinating battle between Afghanistan’s spin trio and Bangladesh’s in-form top order, with Rashid Khan and Noor Ahmad expected to play a central role in choking runs through the middle overs. For Bangladesh, Litton Das remains key, while Tawhid Hridoy and Jaker Ali add depth and balance to the batting lineup. The batters didn't have a great game against the Lankans and will be desperate to turn things around here. Taskin, Mustafizur Rahman, and Tanzim Hasan Sakib will aim to strike early, especially against Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran, who have been game-changers in recent meetings. Historically, Afghanistan have had the upper hand in Asia Cup encounters, winning three of their five clashes against Bangladesh, including a memorable chase in 2022. However, Bangladesh’s 334-run batting masterclass in the 2023 edition showed they have the firepower to dominate as well. Both teams will see this as a pivotal game, with the Afghans eager to show their batting maturity and the Bangla Tigers aiming to prove their consistency. Whose side are you on?
